Course Description | Calculus is a foundational course at Astana IT University; it plays an important role in understanding science, engineering, economics, and computer science, among other disciplines. This Calculus-1 course covers the differentiation and integration of functions of one variable with applications. Course Goal(s) | After completing this course, students should have developed a clear understanding of the fundamental concepts of single-variable calculus and a range of skills that allow them to work effectively with them. The main goal is to be able to apply the tools mentioned above to problems in post-requisite courses. Course Objectives: | Students should study the following concepts:
Sets and functions of one variable
Limits of sequences and their properties
Continuity and properties of continuous functions 
Derivatives and their applications
Antiderivatives and methods to evaluate them
Definite integrals in 1D and 2D cases
Improper integrals
Skills & Competences | After completing this course, students should demonstrate competency in the following skills:
Define the domain and range of the elementary functions
Use both the limit definition and rules of differentiation to differentiate functions. Use L'Hospital's rule to evaluate certain indefinite forms. Sketch the graph of a function using asymptotes, critical points, the derivative test for increasing/decreasing functions, and concavity. Apply differentiation to solve applied max/min problems. Evaluate integrals both by using the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus. Evaluate integrals using integration techniques, such as substitutions and integration by parts. Apply integration to compute arc lengths, volumes of revolution, and surface areas. Determine convergence/divergence of improper integrals and evaluate convergent improper integrals. Course Learning Outcomes: | By the end of this course, students will be able 
to understand concepts related to sets, limits, continuity, derivatives, and basic integrals; 
to apply and work with these concepts numerically, graphically, and analytically; 
apply the tools mentioned above to problems in post-requisite courses. Methods of Assessment | Homework

2. Goals, Objectives and Learning Outcomes of the Course
1. Course This course is an advanced introduction to numerical linear algebra and
Description related numerical methods. Topics include direct and iterative methods
for linear systems, eigenvalue decompositions and LU factorizations,
stability and accuracy of numerical algorithms. Numerical
differentiation and integration. Interpolation. Least squares and
regression analysis. Numerical solution of ordinary differential
equations. Introduction to error analysis. 2. Course Goal(s) The goal of the course is to equip students with the mathematical
knowledge and computational skills necessary to model, analyze, and
solve complex real-world problems. By integrating theoretical concepts
with practical applications, the course aims to foster critical thinking,
enhance problem-solving abilities, and prepare students for advanced
studies or careers in fields such as engineering, data science, finance,
and scientific research. Through hands-on experience with numerical
methods, programming, and mathematical modeling, students will
develop a robust understanding of how to leverage computational tools
to derive meaningful insights from data and mathematical formulations. 3. Course To enhance the problem-solving skills of engineering students using an
Objectives: extremely powerful problem-solving tool namely numerical method. The tool is capable of handling large system of equations, non-linearities
and complicated geometries that are not uncommon in engineering
practice and that are often impossible to solve analytically
4. Skills & • Proficiency in developing numerical algorithms; Competences • Implementing mathematical models through programming
languages; • Analyzing computational errors; • Solving linear and nonlinear equations; • Performing advanced numerical integration; • Creating interpolation techniques; • Designing root-finding strategies; • Applying optimization methods; • Understanding computational complexity; • Critically evaluating mathematical problem-solving approaches
across scientific and engineering domains. 5. Course Learning By the end of this course students will be able to:
Outcomes: • Understand numerical techniques to find the roots of non-linear
equations and solution of system of linear equations. • Use Taylor Series to approximate functions and evaluate the
approximations error. • Program algorithms to locate the roots of nonlinear equations. • Program algorithms to solve linear system of equations. • Smooth engineering collected data using least square method. • Understand the difference operators and the use of
interpolation. • Understand numerical differentiation and integration and
numerical solutions of ordinary differential equations. 6. Methods of The expected learning outcomes for the course will be assessed through

exams, homework, quizzes, and midterms. The ungraded activities will
be used to monitor your progress.

Course Goal(s) | The goal of the course is to equip students with the mathematical knowledge and computational skills necessary to model, analyze, and solve complex real-world problems. By integrating theoretical concepts with practical applications, the course aims to foster critical thinking, enhance problem-solving abilities, and prepare students for advanced studies or careers in fields such as engineering, data science, finance, and scientific research. Through hands-on experience with numerical methods, programming, and mathematical modeling, students will develop a robust understanding of how to leverage computational tools to derive meaningful insights from data and mathematical formulations. Course Objectives: | To enhance the problem-solving skills of engineering students using an extremely powerful problem-solving tool namely numerical method. The tool is capable of handling large system of equations, non-linearities and complicated geometries that are not uncommon in engineering practice and that are often impossible to solve analytically

Methodological Guidelines        
Assessment is administered continuously throughout the course. The students are rated against their performance in continuous rating administered throughout the semester (60%) and summative rating done during the examination session (40%), a total of 100%. Continuous rating is students’ ongoing performance in class and independent work. Classwork is assessed for attendance, laboratory work defense, and in-class assessments. ISIS (Instructor Supervised Student Independent Study) -comprises presentation to be done by students independently and checked by the instructor. Mid-term and End-term is a review of the topics covered and assessment of each student's knowledge. The form of the midterm and end-term exams is complex. Final assessment is a combination of both individual (team) projects (report) and oral presentation (slides) to evaluate the student’s academic performance and professional skills. After completion of this course, each student has to submit an online project version conforming to the project outline, as well as to prepare and present a slide presentation that follows the presentation outline. Project iterations would be required to be submitted as well. Students should submit the written Report of the Final project and slide presentation 3 days before the Final exam day. 2. Goals, Objectives, and Learning Outcomes of the Course | 2. Goals, Objectives, and Learning Outcomes of the Course
Course Description | This course allows students to acquire fundamental knowledge of how computer graphics work on low-level graphics libraries and devices. 2. Goals, Objectives, and Learning Outcomes of the Course | 2. Goals, Objectives, and Learning Outcomes of the Course
Course Description | This course allows students to acquire fundamental knowledge of how computer graphics work on low-level graphics libraries and devices. They will acquire practical skills in programming basic graphical applications using OpenGL. These can be easily scaled to high-level usage of GUI-based engines and graphical applications. Course Goal(s) | The main purpose of this course is to teach students computer graphics techniques and libraries, including theoretical mathematical and algorithmic aspects of computer graphics, and their practical implementation using the modern OpenGL graphics library. Course Objectives: | Define computer graphics and its importance in various industries. Introduce graphics software tools and their roles in the creation and manipulation of images. 2D Graphics
Learn about basic 2D drawing algorithms and techniques. Understand 3D coordinate systems and transformations. Learn about shading models, lighting, and texturing. Introduce graphics programming languages and libraries (e.g., OpenGL or DirectX). Study color theory and color models used in computer graphics. Explore interactive graphics concepts, including user interfaces and event-driven programming. Develop interactive graphics applications and games. Understand the role of computer graphics in multimedia presentations and virtual reality experiences. Apply the knowledge and skills gained throughout the course to complete a substantial graphics project. Skills & Competences | Theoretical knowledge of fundamentals of computer graphics
Theoretical knowledge of modern computer graphics methods and Vulkan
Theoretical knowledge of GPU architecture and usage
Practical skills in the implementation of GPU-accelerated graphics using OpenGL
Practical skills in the usage of basic mathematical methods of lighting, texturing, animation, etc. Course Learning Outcomes: | Upon successful completion of the Computer Graphics Fundamentals course, students will be able to:
Explain the fundamental concepts of computer graphics and its applications across various industries. Identify Graphics Hardware and Software Components:
Recognize and explain the key components of graphics hardware and software, including GPUs, monitors, and graphics APIs. Produce 2D graphics using raster graphics techniques, understanding concepts like pixels, colors, and basic drawing algorithms. Describe the principles of 3D graphics, including 3D modeling, transformations, and rendering. Implement and analyze fundamental graphics algorithms such as line drawing, clipping, and polygon filling. Utilize rasterization and rendering methods for both 2D and 3D graphics, including shading, lighting, and texturing. Develop graphics applications using programming languages and libraries commonly used in computer graphics (e.g., OpenGL, DirectX). Apply matrices and vectors to represent and manipulate graphical data effectively. Demonstrate an understanding of color theory and image processing techniques to enhance and manipulate images.

Course Learning Outcomes: | Upon successful completion of the Computer Graphics Fundamentals course, students will be able to:

Methodological Guidelines        
Assessment is administered continuously throughout the course. The students are rated against their performance in continuous rating administered throughout the semester (60%) and summative rating done during the examination session (40%), total 100%. Continuous rating is students’ on-going performance in class and independent work. Class work is assessed for attendance, laboratory works' defense and in- class assessments. Mid-term and End-term is a review of the topics covered and assessment of each student's knowledge. The form of the midterm and end term exams is complex. Final assessment is a combination of both individual (team) project (report) and oral presentation (slides) to evaluate the students’ academic performance and professional skills. At the completion of this course each student has to submit an online project version conforming to the project outline, as well as to prepare and present a slide presentation that follows the presentation outline. 2. Goals, obiectives and learning outcomes of the course
1. Course This course provides a thorough exploration of data analytics concepts.
description methodologies, and tools, equipping students with the skills necessary to
transform raw data into actionable insights. 2. Course goal(s) - Introduction to Data Analytics: Understand the foundational principles of
data analytics, including types of data. - Data Collection and Preparation: Learn techniques for gathering data from
various sources and the critical steps involved in cleaning and preparing data
for analysis. - Statistical Analysis: Gain proficiency in applying statistical methods to
interpret data, including hypothesis testing, regression analysis, and
correlation. -
Predictive Analytics: Explore advanced analytics techniques such as
machine learning algorithms to forecast future trends and behaviors based
on historical data. - Data Visualization: Master the art of presenting data through effective
visualization techniques using tools Matlab, or Python libraries. - Real-World Applications: Engage in hands-on projects and case studies
that demonstrate how data analytics is applied across various industries,
including finance, healthcare, marketing, and more. 3. Course l. Develop Analytical Skills: Equip students with the ability to collect,
objectives: clean, and prepare data for analysis, enabling them to identify patterns.
trends, and insights that inform decision-making. 2. Apply Statistical Techniques: Enable students to use statistical
methods and tools to analyze data sets effectively, interpret results, and
draw meaningful conclusions that support business objectives. 3. Master Data Visualization and Communication: Teach students how
to create compelling visual representations of data and communicate
insights clearly to stakeholders, ensuring that findings are actionable
and easily understood. Skills l. Data Collection and Preparation:
competences - Ability to gather data from various sources. - Proficiency in data cleaning and preprocessing techniques. 2. Statistical Analysis:
- Understanding of key statistical concepts and methods (e.g.,
hypothesis testing, regression analysis). - Competence in using statistical software (e.g., R, Python, SPSS). 3.Data Visualization:
- Skills in creating informative and visually appealing charts and
graphs using tools like Matlab, or Matplotlib. - Ability to choose appropriate visualization techniques for different
types of data. 4. Critical Thinking:
- Capacity to analyze complex problems, evaluate evidence, and make
data-driven decisions. - Ability to synthesize information from various sources to draw
meaningful conclusions. 5. Communication Skills:
- Proficiency in presenting data insights clearly and persuasively to
diverse audiences. - Ability to write reports that effectively summarize findings and
recommendations. 6. Project Management:
- Skills in planning and executing data analysis projects, managing
timelines, and collaborating with team members. - Ability to prioritize tasks and meet deadlines in a fast-paced
environment. 5.

recurrence relations, graph theory. 2. Course Goal(s) Course goal is to familiarize students with an initial base in mathematics
such as sets, basic of combinatorics and graph theory. The main goal is
to be able to apply above-mentioned tools to problems in postrequisites
courses. 3. Course Course objectives include:

understanding discrete objects); - To solve counting problems using different enumeration methods; - To apply basic techniques involving discrete objects such as sets,
functions, graphs and mathematical expressions in discrete
mathematics; - To develop mathematical abilities in writing programs by computers. 4. Skills & - Basic school mathematical knowledge; Competences - Ability to construct examples and counterexamples
5. Course Learning By the end of this course the students will be able to:
Outcomes: - Know basic mathematical concepts; - Learn main proof techniques of mathematics; - Be familiar with important discrete objects; - Understand counting principles of combinatorics; - Be able to transform discrete problems into simple forms; - Describe programing questions in terms of graphs and trees. 6. 2. Goals, Objectives and Learning Outcomes of the Course
1. Course The course includes logics, set theory, functions, and fundamental
Description principles of counting, number theory, inclusion-exclusion principle,
recurrence relations, graph theory. 2. Course Goal(s) Course goal is to familiarize students with an initial base in mathematics
such as sets, basic of combinatorics and graph theory. The main goal is
to be able to apply above-mentioned tools to problems in postrequisites
courses. 3. Course Course objectives include:
Objectives: - To demonstrate knowledge of mathematical knowledge; - To understand basic mathematical principles (proving, counting,
understanding discrete objects); - To solve counting problems using different enumeration methods; - To apply basic techniques involving discrete objects such as sets,
functions, graphs and mathematical expressions in discrete
mathematics; - To develop mathematical abilities in writing programs by computers. 4. Skills & - Basic school mathematical knowledge; Competences - Ability to construct examples and counterexamples
5. Course Learning By the end of this course the students will be able to:
Outcomes: - Know basic mathematical concepts; - Learn main proof techniques of mathematics; - Be familiar with important discrete objects; - Understand counting principles of combinatorics; - Be able to transform discrete problems into simple forms; - Describe programing questions in terms of graphs and trees. 6. assignments during the academic trimester, one for the 1st attestation

attestation there are going to be 3 lecture quizzes, in total 6 of them. - Midterm, Endterm and Final exams

50 and 80 minutes. During the exams, students are required to
demonstrate their full problem-solving and proof capabilities. Solutions
must be presented step by step, completely, and with academic
accuracy. 7. Reading List 1. Lecture presentations. Main textbooks:

Course description | The course explores foundational algorithms and advanced methodologies in deep reinforcement learning (DRL), emphasizing their applications and impact across various domains of science and technology. Students will gain hands-on experience with state-of-the-art DRL techniques, leveraging neural networks to model complex environments and solve decision-making problems. As an outcome of mastering the course, students will be equipped to design, train, and evaluate DRL models, visualize policy behaviors, analyze performance, and present results effectively, bridging theory with real-world applications. Course objectives | Students will study the following key concepts:
	-	Fundamentals of reinforcement learning and deep reinforcement learning; -	Neural network architectures for reinforcement learning; -	Policy-based and value-based methods; -	Exploration-exploitation trade-offs; -	Model-free and model-based learning approaches; -	Training and evaluation workflows in DRL; -	Applications of DRL in robotics, gaming, and other domains; -	Integration of DRL with computer vision techniques; -	Practical challenges and solutions in DRL implementations. Course goals | The course aims to equip students with both theoretical and practical knowledge in the field of deep reinforcement learning, focusing on the development of algorithms capable of learning and making decisions autonomously in complex environments. Students will gain expertise in creating, implementing, and optimizing DRL models to solve real-world problems across various domains. Skills & Competences | Skills & Competences: Deep Reinforcement Learning
After completing this course, students should demonstrate competency in the following skills:
Proficiency in tools and frameworks for implementing and training deep reinforcement learning models (e.g., TensorFlow, PyTorch, OpenAI Gym). Ability to design and evaluate DRL algorithms, including policy optimization and value function approximation. Competence in analyzing and preprocessing data for DRL applications, including environment modeling and state representation. Expertise in applying DRL to solve problems in robotics, gaming, and other real-world scenarios. Capability to visualize and interpret DRL model performance, detect anomalies, and optimize learning strategies. Course Learning Outcomes | Having completed the course, students will be able to:
Apply practical programming skills to implement deep reinforcement learning algorithms using frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow. Explain the general methodological principles of developing DRL models and integrating them into complex systems. Design, train, and evaluate DRL models for solving tasks in dynamic and uncertain environments. Develop system-level programs for interfacing DRL agents with real-world systems, such as robotics platforms or simulation environments. Optimize DRL algorithms for performance and efficiency in practical applications. 2. Goals, objectives and learning outcomes of the course
Course The course explores foundational algorithms and advanced methodologies
description in deep reinforcement learning (DRL), emphasizing their applications and
impact across various domains of science and technology. Students will gain
hands-on experience with state-of-the-art DRL techniques, leveraging
neural networks to model complex environments and solve decision-making
problems. As an outcome of mastering the course, students will be equipped
to design, train, and evaluate DRL models, visualize policy behaviors,
analyze performance, and present results effectively, bridging theory with
real-world applications. Course Students will study the following key concepts:
objectives - Fundamentals of reinforcement learning and deep
reinforcement learning; - Neural network architectures for reinforcement learning; - Policy-based and value-based methods; - Exploration-exploitation trade-offs; - Model-free and model-based learning approaches; - Training and evaluation workflows in DRL; - Applications of DRL in robotics, gaming, and other domains; - Integration of DRL with computer vision techniques; - Practical challenges and solutions in DRL implementations. Course goals The course aims to equip students with both theoretical and practical
knowledge in the field of deep reinforcement learning, focusing on the
development of algorithms capable of learning and making decisions
autonomously in complex environments. Students will gain expertise in
creating, implementing, and optimizing DRL models to solve real-world
problems across various domains. Skills & Skills & Competences: Deep Reinforcement Learning
Competences After completing this course, students should demonstrate competency in
the following skills:
• Proficiency in tools and frameworks for implementing and training
deep reinforcement learning models (e.g., TensorFlow, PyTorch,
OpenAI Gym). • Ability to design and evaluate DRL algorithms, including policy
optimization and value function approximation. • Competence in analyzing and preprocessing data for DRL
applications, including environment modeling and state
representation. • Expertise in applying DRL to solve problems in robotics, gaming,
and other real-world scenarios. • Capability to visualize and interpret DRL model performance, detect
anomalies, and optimize learning strategies. Course Having completed the course, students will be able to:
Learning • Apply practical programming skills to implement deep reinforcement
Outcomes learning algorithms using frameworks such as PyTorch or
TensorFlow. • Explain the general methodological principles of developing DRL
models and integrating them into complex systems. • Design, train, and evaluate DRL models for solving tasks in dynamic
and uncertain environments. • Develop system-level programs for interfacing DRL agents with real-
world systems, such as robotics platforms or simulation
environments. • Optimize DRL algorithms for performance and efficiency in practical
applications. Methods of The expected learning outcomes for the course will be assessed through

1. Course Finite Volume\Element method is the mainstay in many engineering
Description fields. This course aims to provide a preliminary finite element basis
knowledge which can be extended further for more sophisticated real-
life applications. 2. Course Goal(s) (1) To understand major numerical methods for PDEs and the associated
computer implementation
(2) To be able to apply the numerical methods to solve a variety of linear
science and engineering
problems with hand calculations and computer simulations
(3) To be able to apply the numerical methods for solutions of some
nonlinear problems
(4) To be able to complete a course project with a written report and
conduct presentations
3. Course Numerical solution of the PDEs are of great importance to be
Objectives: solved to leverage the benefits of the accurate simulations. It is
commonality that many nonlinear PDEs cannot be solved in their closed
form, as semi-linear or nonlinear problems might describe the natural
phenomenon which happen in real life. Therefore, it is crucial to develop
an accurate and stable numerical solution for various type of modelling
problem found in different applied fields such as: Finance, Mechanical
engineering, Aerospace engineering, Fluid dynamics, Heat transfer,
Mathematical biology and many more. 4. Skills & • Construction of the discretizations in time and space directions
Competences • Implementation of the Fintie Element subroutines via high and
low level programming languages
• Option pricing applications, such as Black Scholes to be solved by
FEM and FDM
• Creation of the uniform and nonuniform meshes with variable step
sizes in both temporal and spatial directions. 5. Course Learning Finite Volume satisfies the university core curriculum requirement in

Course Description | This course offers an in-depth exploration of fuzzy logic, neural networks, and their applications within the realm of machine learning. Students will begin by understanding the foundational concepts of fuzzy logic, fuzzy sets, and fuzzy reasoning. The course will then delve into fuzzy clustering techniques and introduce the fundamentals of neural networks, including advanced models like deep learning neural networks. Additionally, students will learn about the integration of genetic algorithms with fuzzy and neural systems, including genetic-fuzzy and neuro-fuzzy systems. The final part of the course will focus on soft computing techniques and computational intelligence, which combine various methods to solve complex real-world problems effectively. Course Goal(s) | To provide a comprehensive understanding of fuzzy logic and its applications in machine learning. To introduce students to the concepts and methodologies involved in combining neural networks, genetic algorithms, and fuzzy logic. To develop practical skills in designing and implementing soft computing techniques for real-world problems. Course Objectives: | Understand the foundational principles of fuzzy logic and its significance in artificial intelligence. Learn how to construct and manipulate fuzzy sets. Develop proficiency in fuzzy reasoning and its applications. Gain insights into fuzzy clustering techniques and their practical implementations. Understand the fundamentals of neural networks, including various architectures and training algorithms. Explore advanced neural network models like deep learning. Study the integration of fuzzy systems with genetic algorithms and neural networks. Apply neuro-fuzzy systems to solve complex computational problems. Gain knowledge in soft computing and computational intelligence methodologies. Skills & Competences | Mastery of fuzzy logic principles and reasoning techniques. Competence in designing and applying fuzzy clustering algorithms. Proficiency in constructing and training different types of neural networks. Ability to implement and integrate genetic algorithms with fuzzy and neural systems. Critical thinking skills in analyzing and developing computational intelligence applications. Practical skills in applying machine learning and fuzzy logic to real-world problems. Course Learning Outcomes: | By the end of this course students will be able to:
Understand and apply the principles of fuzzy logic in various contexts. Construct and manipulate fuzzy sets and apply fuzzy reasoning techniques. Implement fuzzy clustering algorithms for data analysis. Design and train different types of neural networks, including deep learning models. Develop and integrate genetic-fuzzy and genetic-neural systems. Implement neuro-fuzzy systems to solve complex problems. Apply soft computing techniques and computational intelligence in various domains. Methods of Assessment | Assignments

2. Goals, Objectives and Learning Outcomes of the Course
1. Course Introduction to Optimization Theory plays a critical role in
Description understanding a wide range of fields, including economics, engineering,
data science, machine learning, and operations research. This course
covers the fundamental concepts and methods in optimization,
including the mathematical formulation of optimization problems,
linear and nonlinear optimization techniques, and constrained
optimization. 2. Course Goal(s) After completing this course, students should have developed a clear
understanding of the fundamental concepts in optimization theory and
a range of skills that allow them to effectively solve optimization
problems. The main goal is to be able to apply optimization techniques,
including linear programming, gradient methods, and constrained
optimization, to problems in post-requisite courses. 3. Course  To introduce students to the basic principles and techniques in
Objectives: optimization theory, including the formulation and classification of
optimization problems.  To equip students with the skills necessary to analyze and solve
linear and nonlinear optimization problems, both with and without
constraints.  To provide students with practical experience in applying
optimization algorithms, such as the Simplex method for linear
programming, gradient descent for unconstrained optimization, and
Lagrange multipliers for constrained optimization.  To familiarize students with convex optimization problems and the
associated theory, including duality and optimality conditions, to
streamline the problem-solving process. 4. Skills &  Proficiency in transforming word problems into mathematical
Competences optimization problems, both linear and nonlinear.  Mastery of optimization algorithms, including the Simplex
method for linear programming, gradient descent for
unconstrained optimization, and techniques for solving
constrained optimization problems.  Familiarity with solving convex optimization problems and using
duality to simplify complex problems.  Ability to critically assess the structure of optimization problems
and identify appropriate solution methods based on the problem’s
nature (e.g., linearity, convexity, and constraints).  Capability to analyze the feasibility and optimality conditions of
an optimization problem and interpret the results accurately.  Ability to identify potential issues, such as non-convergence or
local optima, and take corrective actions or make informed
decisions about solution reliability. 5. Course Learning By the end of this course students will be able to:
Outcomes:  Translate real-world problems into mathematical optimization
models, identifying objective functions, constraints, and decision
variables in both linear and nonlinear contexts.  Apply the Simplex method and other algorithms to solve linear
programming problems and interpret the results effectively.  Use gradient-based methods (e.g., gradient descent) to solve
unconstrained optimization problems and understand their
convergence properties.  Utilize methods like Lagrange multipliers and the Karush-Kuhn-
Tucker (KKT) conditions to solve optimization problems with
constraints.

Course Description | The course covers systems of linear equations, matrices, inverse of a matrix, determinant, vectors in two-, three- and n-dimensions, vector spaces and subspaces, eigenvectors and eigenspaces, and applications of linear algebra
Course Goal(s) | To provide students with the knowledge of fundamentals of linear algebra and the theory of matrices. On completion of this course the student will master the basic concepts and acquires skills in solving problems in linear algebra
Course Objectives | Comprehend vector spaces and subspaces. Understand fundamental properties of matrices including determinants, inverse matrices, matrix factorizations, eigenvalues, and linear transformations. Solve linear systems of equations
Skills & Competences | Ability to write mathematical statements and problem solutions using mathematical symbols;
understanding of key mathematical concepts and the application of appropriate tools to real problems; Writing logical progressions of precise mathematical statements to justify and communicate your reasoning
Course Learning Outcomes | By the end of this course students will be able to:
Use Gauss-Jordan elimination to solve systems of linear equations and to compute the inverse of an invertible matrix. Use the basic concepts of vector and matrix algebra, including linear dependence / independence, basis and dimension of a subspace, rank, and nullity, for analysis of matrices and systems of linear equations. Evaluate determinants and use them to discriminate between singular and nonsingular matrices. Use the characteristic polynomial to compute the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a square matrix and use them to diagonalize matrices when this is possible. Combine methods of matrix algebra to compose the change-of-basis matrix with respect to two bases of a vector space

Course Description | The course covers systems of linear equations, matrices, inverse of a matrix, determinant, vectors in two-, three- and n-dimensions, vector spaces and subspaces, eigenvectors and eigenspaces, and applications of linear algebra
Course Goal(s) | To provide students with the knowledge of fundamentals of linear algebra and the theory of matrices. On completion of this course the student will master the basic concepts and acquires skills in solving problems in linear algebra
Course Objectives | Comprehend vector spaces and subspaces. Understand fundamental properties of matrices including determinants, inverse matrices, matrix factorizations, eigenvalues, and linear transformations. Solve linear systems of equations
Skills & Competences | Ability to write mathematical statements and problem solutions using mathematical symbols;
understanding of key mathematical concepts and the application of appropriate tools to real problems; Writing  logical progressions of precise mathematical statements to justify and communicate your reasoning
Course Learning Outcomes | By the end of this course students will be able to:
Use Gauss-Jordan elimination to solve systems of linear equations and to compute the inverse of an invertible matrix. Use the basic concepts of vector and matrix algebra, including linear dependence / independence, basis and dimension of a subspace, rank, and nullity, for analysis of matrices and systems of linear equations. Evaluate determinants and use them to discriminate between singular and nonsingular matrices. Use the characteristic polynomial to compute the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a square matrix and use them to diagonalize matrices when this is possible. Combine methods of matrix algebra to compose the change-of-basis matrix with respect to two bases of a vector space

Course Description | The course covers systems of linear equations, matrices, inverse of a matrix, determinant, vectors in two-, three- and n-dimensions, vector spaces and subspaces, eigenvectors and eigenspaces, and applications of linear algebra
Course Goal(s) | To provide students with the knowledge of fundamentals of linear algebra and the theory of matrices. On completion of this course the student will master the basic concepts and acquires skills in solving problems in linear algebra
Course Objectives | Comprehend vector spaces and subspaces. Understand fundamental properties of matrices including determinants, inverse matrices, matrix factorizations, eigenvalues, and linear transformations. Solve linear systems of equations
Skills & Competences | ability to write mathematical statements and problem solutions using mathematical symbols;
understanding of key mathematical concepts and the application of appropriate tools to real problems; Writing logical progressions of precise mathematical statements to justify and communicate your reasoning
Course Learning Outcomes | By the end of this course students will be able to:
Use Gauss-Jordan elimination to solve systems of linear equations and to compute the inverse of an invertible matrix. Use the basic concepts of vector and matrix algebra, including linear dependence / independence, basis and dimension of a subspace, rank, and nullity, for analysis of matrices and systems of linear equations. Evaluate determinants and use them to discriminate between singular and nonsingular matrices.

understanding of key mathematical concepts and the application of appropriate tools to real problems; Writing  logical progressions of precise mathematical statements to justify and communicate your reasoning
Course Learning Outcomes | By the end of this course students will be able to:
Use Gauss-Jordan elimination to solve systems of linear equations and to compute the inverse of an invertible matrix. Use the basic concepts of vector and matrix algebra, including linear dependence / independence, basis and dimension of a subspace, rank, and nullity, for analysis of matrices and systems of linear equations. Evaluate determinants and use them to discriminate between singular and nonsingular matrices. Use the characteristic polynomial to compute the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a square matrix and use them to diagonalize matrices when this is possible. Combine methods of matrix algebra to compose the change-of-basis matrix with respect to two bases of a vector space

1. Course The course covers systems of linear equations, matrices, inverse of a
Description matrix, determinant, vectors in two-, three- and n-dimensions, vector

algebra and the theory of matrices. On completion of this course the

Course Description | This course provides a comprehensive introduction to the fundamental concepts and techniques of machine learning and artificial intelligence. Students will explore a range of topics, from classical machine learning algorithms to modern deep learning architectures, and gain practical experience in applying these methods to real-world problems. We will cover the theoretical underpinnings of various AI and ML approaches, alongside hands-on implementation and evaluation using popular programming languages and libraries. Course Goal(s) |   Provide a foundational understanding: Equip students with the core principles and concepts of machine learning and artificial intelligence.   Develop practical skills: Enable students to apply various machine learning algorithms and deep learning techniques to solve real-world problems. Course Objectives: | Understand the core principles and applications of machine learning and artificial intelligence. Apply various supervised and unsupervised learning algorithms to solve prediction and pattern recognition tasks. Design and implement neural networks for deep learning applications. Evaluate the performance of machine learning models and select appropriate algorithms for specific problems. Understand the ethical considerations and societal impact of AI. Utilize popular machine learning libraries and tools (e.g., Python, scikit-learn, TensorFlow, PyTorch). Develop practical skills in data preprocessing, feature engineering, model training, and evaluation. Skills & Competences | Ability to utilize machine learning libraries (scikit-learn, TensorFlow, PyTorch). Understanding and application of linear algebra, calculus, probability, and statistics in machine learning. Practical experience in implementing supervised and unsupervised learning algorithms. Ability to design and train neural networks for deep learning. Course Learning Outcomes: | By the end of this course students will be able to:
Students will be able to define and explain fundamental concepts like supervised learning, unsupervised learning, reinforcement learning, neural networks, and deep learning. Students will be able to describe and differentiate between various algorithms, such as linear regression, logistic regression, decision trees, support vector machines, and k-means clustering. Students will be able to understand the mathematical principles behind machine learning algorithms, including linear algebra, calculus, and probability. Students will be able to use programming languages like Python and libraries like scikit-learn, TensorFlow, or PyTorch to implement and apply machine learning algorithms. Students will be able to train machine learning models using appropriate datasets and evaluate their performance using relevant metrics. Methods of Assessment | Practical implementation and presentation

Methodological Guidelines        
Assessment is administered continuously throughout the course. The students are rated against their performance in continuous rating administered throughout the semester (60%) and summative rating done during the examination session (40%), total 100%. Continuous rating is students’ on-going performance in class and independent work. Class work is assessed for attendance, laboratory works' defense and in- class assessments. ISIS (Instructor Supervised Student Independent Study) -comprises presentation to be done by students independently and checked by instructor. Mid-term and End-term is a review of the topics covered and assessment of each student's knowledge. The form of the midterm and end term exams is complex. Final assessment is a combination of both individual (team) project (report) and oral presentation (slides) to evaluate the students’ academic performance and professional skills. At the completion of this course each student has to submit an online project version conforming to the project outline, as well as to prepare and present a slide presentation that follows the presentation outline. second-order linear differential equation with various boundary
conditions are considered. Convergence of approximate methods is

Course Description | Mathematics for Computational Science is a core course at Astana IT University; it plays an important role in understanding science, technology, economics, and computer science, among other disciplines. This course, Mathematics for Computational Science, covers difference derivatives, algorithms, and methods for solving the Cauchy problem for a first-order linear differential equation. It discusses various methods for solving a second-order linear differential equation with different boundary conditions. For the problems under consideration, it studies methods for solving various inverse problems. It investigates the convergence of iterative processes for solving the inverse problem. And it determines the convergence rate of the iterative processes. Course Goal(s) | Mathematics for Computational Science is a core course at Astana IT University; it plays an important role in understanding science, technology, economics, and computer science, among other disciplines. This course, Mathematics for Computational Science, covers difference derivatives, algorithms, and methods for solving the Cauchy problem for a first-order linear differential equation. Methods for solving a second-order linear differential equation with various boundary conditions are considered. Convergence of approximate methods is numerically verified. Algorithms for solving the problem are created. For the problems under consideration, methods for solving various inverse problems are studied. Convergence of iterative processes for solving the inverse problem is investigated. And the convergence rate of the iterative processes is determined. Course Objectives: | Postgraduate students should master the following concepts
• Exact solution of linear differential equations of the first order. Solution of the inverse problem. Method, algorithm and program. • Exact solution of linear differential equations of the second order. Solution of the inverse problem. Boundary conditions: Dirichlet, Neumann and shifted boundary conditions. Method, algorithm and program. • Approximate solution of nonlinear differential equations of the second order. Solution of the inverse problem. Boundary conditions: Dirichlet, Neumann and shifted boundary conditions. Method, algorithm and program
Skills & Competences | Upon completion of this course, graduate students should demonstrate competence in the following inverse problem solving skills:
• Method of finding unknown parameters of processes described by first-order linear differential equations. Algorithm and program. • Method of finding unknown parameters of a process described by second-order linear differential equations under various boundary conditions. Algorithm and program. • Method of finding unknown parameters of a process described by second-order nonlinear differential equations. Algorithm and program.

Solution of the inverse problem. Boundary conditions: Dirichlet, Neumann and shifted boundary conditions. Method, algorithm and program

Algorithm and program. • Method of finding unknown parameters of a process described by second-order nonlinear differential equations. Algorithm and program. - finding unknown parameters of a process described by first-order linear differential equations.

Course Description | “Natural Language Processing” is a 10-week course, Natural language processing (NLP) or computational linguistics is one of the most important technologies of the information age. Applications of NLP are everywhere because people communicate almost everything in language: web search, advertising, emails, customer service, language translation, virtual agents, medical reports, politics, etc. In the last decade, deep learning (or neural network) approaches have obtained very high performance across many different NLP tasks, using single end-to-end neural models that do not require traditional, task-specific feature engineering. In this course, students will gain a thorough introduction to cutting-edge research in Deep Learning for NLP. Through lectures, assignments and a final project, students will learn the necessary skills to design, implement, and understand their own neural network models, using the Pytorch framework. Course Goal(s) | Key elements of this course include:
The most important algorithms in NLP
Fundamental concepts needed to reason about learning algorithms Techniques for implementing and deploying NLP in practice

to study word embeddings and text classification methods;
to learn Language Modelling;
to study basic architectures of attention based models;
to study LLMS and Prompting.
to apply Transfer learning  for LLM Models. Skills & Competences | Completing an NLP course equips students with foundational knowledge in linguistics, machine learning, and programming. Key skills include text processing, feature engineering, and proficiency in NLP frameworks. Students gain expertise in named entity recognition, sentiment analysis, and deep learning techniques like RNNs and Transformers. Ethical considerations and project management skills are emphasized. This prepares individuals for diverse career paths, such as working on cutting-edge NLP products, industry roles in deep learning, or advanced studies in data science or deep learning research. Course Learning Outcomes: | Upon completing the NLP course, students will:
Apply ML judiciously in NLP, choosing suitable algorithms. Master data gathering and preprocessing for robust NLP models. Understand end-to-end ML training and evaluation for NLP tasks. Proficiently code in Python using Pytorch and Hugging Face for NLP applications. Innovate by proposing, designing, and executing experiments for product or research ideas. Communicate effectively, presenting findings and demos to diverse audiences, enhancing professional collaboration and presentation skills.

1 | Word Embeddings. Word embeddings. Distributional semantics. Count-based (pre-neural) methods. Word2Vec: learn vectors. GloVe: count, then learn. Evaluation: intrinsic vs extrinsic. Analysis and Interpretability. | 2 | 2
2 | Text Classification
Text classification: introduction and datasets. General framework: feature extractor + classifier. Classical approaches: Naive Bayes, MaxEnt (Logistic Regression), SVM. Neural Networks: General View, Convolutional Models, Recurrent Models. Practical Tips: Data Augmentation. Analysis and Interpretability. | 2 | 2
3 | Language Modeling. Language Modeling: what does it mean? Left-to-right framework. N-gram language models. Neural Language Models: General View, Recurrent Models, Convolutional Models. Evaluation. Practical Tips: Weight Tying. Analysis and Interpretability. | 2 | 2
4 | Seq2seq and Attention. Seq2seq Basics: Encoder-Decoder framework, Training, Simple Models, Inference (e.g., beam search). Attention: general, score functions, models. | 2 | 2
5 | Transformers. Transformer: self-attention, masked self-attention, multi-head attention; model architecture. Subword Segmentation (BPE). Analysis and Interpretability: functions of attention heads; probing for linguistic structure. | 2 | 2

Course Description | Calculus is a foundational course at Astana IT University; it plays an important role in the understanding of science, engineering, economics, and computer science, among other disciplines. This Calculus course covers differentiation and integration of functions of one and multiple variables, with applications. Topics include:
Concepts of Function, Limits and Continuity
Differentiation Rules, Applications, Rates, Approximations, and Extremum Problems
Definite and Indefinite Integration
The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
Applications to Geometry: Area, Volume, and Arc Length
Techniques of Integration 
Approximation of Definite Integrals, Improper Integrals, and L'Hôspital's Rule
Multivariable functions, scalar field
Gradient and its properties
Applications
Double and concept of multidimensional integrals
Course Goal(s) | After completing this course, students should have developed a clear understanding of the fundamental concepts of single and multivariable variable calculus and a range of skills allowing them to work effectively with the concepts. The main goal is to be able to apply above-mentioned tools to problems in postrequisites courses. Course Objectives: | After completing this course, students should demonstrate competency in the following skills:
Use both the limit definition and rules of differentiation to differentiate functions. Sketch the graph of a function using asymptotes, critical points, the derivative test for increasing/decreasing functions, and concavity. Apply differentiation to solve applied max/min problems. Apply differentiation to solve related rates problems. Evaluate integrals by using the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus. Evaluate integrals using substitution and integration by parts. Use L'Hospital's rule to evaluate certain indefinite forms. Determine convergence/divergence of improper integrals and evaluate convergent improper integrals. Compute the gradient of the multidimensional function. Evaluate elementary double integrals and apply them to compute areas and volumes. Skills & Competences
Course Learning Outcomes: | The successful Calculus student should understand and be able to apply concepts related to limits, continuity, derivatives and basic integrals. The student should be able to work with these concepts numerically, graphically and analytically. Methods of Assessment | Homework

Course Description | Numerical Methods for Differential Equations - basic course at Astana IT University; it plays an important role in understanding science, technology, economics, and computer science, as well as other disciplines. This course, Numerical Methods for Differential Equations, covers algorithms and methods for solving the Cauchy problem, boundary value problems, and other problems posed for differential equations. Course Goal(s) | Purpose of the course
The goal of the course is that upon completion of the course, students will be able to recognize and master from a user's perspective the concepts and fundamental computational methods for differential equations. Course objectives:
● Introduce the basic ideas of numerical methods for differential equations, including numerical methods for solving problems of ordinary differential equations and problems of partial differential equations. ● Apply fundamental concepts of numerical methods to differential equations in a variety of applications.

• Numerical methods for solving elliptic type problems. • Numerical methods for solving hyperbolic type problems. Numerical methods for solving parabolic type problems. Skills & Competences | Upon completion of this course, students must demonstrate competency in the following skills:

Course Description | Numerical Methods is a core course at Astana IT University; it plays an important role in understanding science, technology, economics and computer science, as well as other disciplines. This course, Numerical Methods , covers difference derivatives, algorithms and methods for solving the Cauchy problem for differential equations, interpolation problems, approximate methods for calculating definite integrals, approximate methods for solving systems of linear algebraic equations, solving nonlinear and systems of nonlinear algebraic equations. Course Goal(s) | The objective of the course is that upon completion of the course, students will be able to use computational methods for solving SLAE and NSLAE. Recognize and master from a user's perspective the concepts and basic computational methods of algebra and analysis. Course Objectives: ● Introduce the basic ideas of numerical methods of algebra and analysis, including computational methods for solving SLAE and NSLAE. ● Apply the basic concepts of numerical methods of algebra and analysis to various applications. Course Learning Outcomes Students who successfully complete the course will be able to: 
● Solve real-world algebra and analysis processes numerically (using a computer), . ● Create algorithms and codes for solving real-world algebra and analysis processes. Course Objectives: | Students should learn the following concepts: • Solution of a system of linear algebraic equations (SLAE). Method, algorithm and program. • Solution of a system of nonlinear algebraic equations (SNAE). Method, algorithm and program. • Splines of the first, second and third order. Convergence, algorithm and program. • Numerical methods for calculating definite integrals. Convergence, algorithm and program. Numerical methods for solving the Cauchy problem for an ordinary differential equation (ODE). Convergence, algorithm and program. Skills & Competences | Upon completion of this course, students should demonstrate competence in the following skills in solving algebra and analysis problems:
• Method of checking the convergence and stability of numerical methods for solving SLAE problems; • Method of checking the convergence of numerical methods for solving SNAE problems; • Method of checking the stability of numerical methods for solving interpolation problems; • Approximate method for calculating definite integrals. Checking the convergence of approximate methods. Course Learning Outcomes: | By the end of this course, students will be able to understand concepts related to algebra and analysis problems, namely, numerical methods for solving SLAE, SNAE, interpolation problems, approximate methods for solving the Cauchy problem for ODE, approximate calculations of definite integrals. The student should be able to establish the convergence and stability of the studied approximate methods.

Course Description | Quantum computing is a multidisciplinary field comprising aspects of computer science, physics, and mathematics that utilizes quantum mechanics to solve complex problems faster than on classical computers. The field of quantum computing includes hardware research and application development. Quantum computing is a revolutionary area of computer science that leverages the principles of quantum mechanics to process information in ways that classical computers cannot. Unlike traditional computers, which use binary digits (bits) to represent data as either 0 or 1, quantum computers use quantum bits, or qubits, which can represent 0, 1, or both simultaneously due to a quantum property called superposition.

Course Description | Quantum computing is a multidisciplinary field comprising aspects of computer science, physics, and mathematics that utilizes quantum mechanics to solve complex problems faster than on classical computers. The field of quantum computing includes hardware research and application development. Quantum computing is a revolutionary area of computer science that leverages the principles of quantum mechanics to process information in ways that classical computers cannot. Unlike traditional computers, which use binary digits (bits) to represent data as either 0 or 1, quantum computers use quantum bits, or qubits, which can represent 0, 1, or both simultaneously due to a quantum property called superposition. Course Goal(s) | The goals of a quantum computing course typically focus on providing students with the knowledge and skills necessary to understand the fundamentals of quantum computing and how to apply them in real-world scenarios. Course Objectives: | Course objectives include: 
1. Understand Quantum Mechanics Principles
Students should be able to describe quantum phenomena and recognize their importance in quantum computing. 2. Learn the Basics of Quantum Computing
Students should understand how quantum bits (qubits) work, including quantum gates, quantum states, and the idea of quantum circuits. 3. Explore Quantum Algorithms
Students should learn about algorithms such as Shor’s algorithm for factoring large numbers, Grover's algorithm for search, and quantum simulations. 4. Understand Quantum Error Correction  
Students should understand how quantum error correction works and why it's critical for building reliable quantum computers. Skills & Competences | - Apply advanced mathematics, including linear algebra, complex numbers, and probability theory, to solve quantum computing problems. Work with matrix operations and vector spaces. Analyze quantum states and transformations using mathematical frameworks. - Evaluate the feasibility and efficiency of quantum solutions to various problems. Break down complex systems into manageable quantum components. Identify when quantum computing provides an advantage over classical methods. Course Learning Outcomes: | By the end of the quantum computing course, students should achieve the following learning outcomes:
1. Understanding Quantum Mechanics Principles
Demonstrate a foundational understanding of quantum mechanics concepts such as superposition, entanglement, and quantum measurement. 2. Quantum Information Fundamentals
Explain the difference between classical and quantum information processing, and describe the role of qubits, quantum gates, and quantum circuits. 3. Familiarity with Quantum Algorithms
Understand and describe major quantum algorithms
4. Quantum Error Correction
Analyze the challenges of quantum noise and decoherence and explain quantum error correction techniques.

Methodological Guidelines        
Assessment is administered continuously throughout the course. The students are rated against their performance in continuous rating administered throughout the semester (60%) and summative rating done during the examination session (40%), total 100%. Continuous rating is students’ on-going performance in class and independent work. Class work is assessed for attendance, laboratory works' defense and in- class assessments. ISIS (Instructor Supervised Student Independent Study) -comprises presentation to be done by students independently and checked by instructor. Mid-term and End-term is a review of the topics covered and assessment of each student's knowledge. The form of the midterm and end term exams is complex. Final assessment is a combination of both individual (team) project (report) and oral presentation (slides) to evaluate the students’ academic performance and professional skills. At the completion of this course each student has to submit an online project version conforming to the project outline, as well as to prepare and present a slide presentation that follows the presentation outline. Course Description | This course offers a comprehensive exploration of how to optimize the performance of parallel computing systems, ranging from small multi-core processors to large-scale computing clusters. Key topics include parallel architecture design, efficient resource management, and strategies for optimizing memory access. Students will learn to analyze and design parallel algorithms, utilizing advanced programming techniques that can be applied across various hardware platforms. The course also emphasizes performance benchmarking and scalability analysis, enabling students to assess the effectiveness of their parallel implementations in diverse real-world applications. Course Goal(s) | Understand Parallel Computing Architectures
Design and Implement Efficient Parallel Algorithms
Master Parallel Programming Tools and Techniques
Optimize Performance of Computational Applications
Apply High-Performance Computing to Real-World Problems
Evaluate and Benchmark Parallel Solutions
Course Objectives: | Understand parallel computing concepts. Analyze parallel system architectures. Design and develop parallel algorithms. Use parallel programming models and tools. Optimize memory access and performance. Assess scalability and efficiency of parallel solutions. Skills & Competences | Proficiency in parallel programming languages (OpenCL, CUDA, MPI). Ability to design efficient parallel algorithms. Competence in optimizing memory access and data flow in parallel systems. Skills in analyzing and benchmarking performance of parallel applications. Understanding of CPU and GPU architectures for high-performance computing. Ability to solve complex computational problems using parallelism. Knowledge of load balancing, synchronization, and task scheduling. Expertise in debugging and optimizing parallel code. Familiarity with performance profiling tools and techniques. Capability to implement scalable solutions on multi-core and distributed systems. Course Learning Outcomes: | By the end of this course students will be able to:
Explain the principles and architectures of modern parallel computing systems. Design and implement parallel algorithms for multi-core CPUs and GPUs. Utilize parallel programming frameworks such as OpenCL, CUDA, and MPI effectively. Optimize parallel programs for performance, including memory management and data distribution. Analyze the scalability and efficiency of parallel solutions in various computing environments. Solve computationally intensive problems using advanced parallel processing techniques. Evaluate and benchmark the performance of parallel applications across different hardware platforms. Methods of Assessment | Assignments

Solve a first-order linear ODE by the methods of integrating factors and  variation of parameters. Model a simple system to obtain a first-order ODE. Recreate the phase portrait of a two-dimensional linear autonomous system from trace and determinant. Academic Year 2024-2025
1. General Information
Course title Big Data and Distributed Algorithms
Degree cycle (level)/ Bachelor degree / 6B06103 Big Data Analysis
major
Year, term Year 3, Term 2
Number of credits 5
Language of English
delivery:
Prerequisites “Big Data and Distributed Algorithms” is based on knowledge obtained
by the students on Information and Communication Technologies,
Database Management Systems, Computer Organisation and
Architecture, Machine Learning, Cloud Computing, and Operating
Systems and Computer Networks courses. Postrequisites Knowledge obtained during the course will be used for big data analysis
and performing research on data analytics. Lecturer(s) Yermek Alimzhanov, senior lecturer,
ermek.alimzhanov@astanait.edu.kz
Astana IT University, Expo, C1 block, 3d floor, office C1.2.327. 2. Goals, Objectives and Learning Outcomes of the Course
1. Course This course introduces you to the core concepts of big data processing
Description and analytics. The course helps learners develop skills with cloud
services that are critical for conducting analysis of big data problems. This course is intended for students who seek expertise on the tasks,
tools, and strategies that are used to collect, store, prepare, analyze, and
visualize data for use in analytics and ML applications. This course is
most aligned to a data engineer role but would also be appropriate for
data analysts; data scientists; extract, transform, and load (ETL)
developers; or ML practitioners who want to understand how the data
that they use in their analyses and predictions is prepared for analysis. The course will also familiarize you with some distributed algorithms
and their application areas. You will learn about important big data storage and processing
frameworks like Apache Hadoop, Apache Spark, and other software
packages of Hadoop ecosystem. 2. Course Goal(s) This course is designed to give students a detailed overview of methods
and tools for Big Data collection, storage, processing, and analysis. Throughout the course, students will explore use cases from real-world
applications, which will enable them to make informed decisions while
building data pipelines for their applications. The goal of the course is
to introduce the students to important basic concepts of Big Data
analytics and provide practice to obtain a better understanding of the
problems. This creates a basis for the students to learn more advanced
concepts and other technologies in more details in preparation either for
a job in industry or for the following courses at the graduate level. 3. Course You will learn:
Objectives:
1. About Big Data and its elements (the five Vs of data). 2. How to design modern data pipeline architecture. 3. On securing and scaling the data pipeline. 4. How to perform ETL by batch or by stream data. 5. Storing and analyzing data using Apache Hadoop framework. 6. Big data processing and analytics with Apache Spark. 7. The machine learning (ML) concepts and lifecycle. 8. Data visualization tools and services. 9. What are distributed systems and algorithms? 10. Preliminary examples of Distributed algorithms and their
applications. 4. Skills & This course requires a strong foundation in IT concepts and skills.

- Experience with cloud services (AWS, GCP, etc.). - Worked with databases and Structured Query Language (SQL). - Operating systems and command line interface (Linux, bash,

probability, and statistics. 5. Course Learning By the end of this course students will be able to:
Outcomes: • Summarize the role and value of data science in a data-driven
organization. • Recognize how the elements of data influence decisions about
the infrastructure of a data pipeline. • Illustrate a data pipeline by using cloud services to meet a
generalized use case. • Identify scaling considerations and best practices for building
pipelines that handle large-scale datasets. • Design and build a data collection process while considering
constraints such as scalability, cost, fault tolerance, and latency. • Implement the steps to process structured, semistructured, and
unstructured data formats in a data pipeline. • Explain the concept of MapReduce and how Apache Hadoop is
used in big data analytics. • Analyze data by using open-source tools that are appropriate to a
given use case. 6. Methods of The expected learning outcomes for the course will be assessed

Course Description | Calculus is a foundational course at Astana IT University; it plays an important role in understanding science, engineering, economics, and computer science, among other disciplines. This Calculus-1 course covers the differentiation and integration of functions of one variable with applications. Course Goal(s) | After completing this course, students should have developed a clear understanding of the fundamental concepts of single-variable calculus and a range of skills that allow them to work effectively with them. The main goal is to be able to apply the tools mentioned above to problems in post-requisite courses. Course Objectives: | Students should study the following concepts:
Sets and functions of one variable
Limits of sequences and their properties
Continuity and properties of continuous functions 
Derivatives and their applications
Antiderivatives and methods to evaluate them
Definite integrals in 1D and 2D cases
Improper integrals
Skills & Competences | After completing this course, students should demonstrate competency in the following skills:
Define the domain and range of the elementary functions
Use both the limit definition and rules of differentiation to differentiate functions. Use L'Hospital's rule to evaluate certain indefinite forms. Sketch the graph of a function using asymptotes, critical points, the derivative test for increasing/decreasing functions, and concavity. Apply differentiation to solve applied max/min problems. Evaluate integrals both by using the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus. Evaluate integrals using integration techniques, such as substitutions and integration by parts. Apply integration to compute arc lengths, volumes of revolution, and surface areas. Determine convergence/divergence of improper integrals and evaluate convergent improper integrals. to understand concepts related to sets, limits, continuity, derivatives, and basic integrals; 
to apply and work with these concepts numerically, graphically, and analytically;

Students will explore different neural network architectures, including CNNs and RNNs, and apply them to solve tasks like classification and regression. The course provides hands-on experience in building, training, and optimizing models using techniques like gradient descent. Students will also learn to evaluate model performance and apply neural networks to real-world problems, preparing them for advanced topics in AI and machine learning. Course Goal(s) | The goal of this course is to provide students with a solid foundation in neural network theory and practice, enabling them to build, train, and optimize various neural network models. By the end of the course, students will be able to apply neural networks to solve complex tasks such as classification and regression, evaluate model performance, and effectively address real-world problems in artificial intelligence and machine learning. This course will also prepare students for more advanced topics in AI and neural network applications. Course Objectives: | Having completed the course, the student will:
Understand key concepts such as activation functions, loss functions, and backpropagation. Explore and differentiate between various neural network types, including CNNs and RNNs. Apply neural networks to solve classification and regression tasks. Optimize and train networks using techniques like gradient descent. Evaluate model performance using appropriate metrics. Implement neural networks for real-world applications across various domains. Skills & Competences | Machine Learning:
Proficiency in deep learning, neural network architectures, and gradient-based optimization. Experience with overfitting prevention, training techniques, and hyperparameter tuning. Programming and Tools:
Expertise in Python and frameworks like TensorFlow or PyTorch. Knowledge of automatic differentiation for computing derivatives. Experience with physics simulators or modeling tools. Problem Solving and Analytical Thinking:
Ability to translate physics problems into machine learning frameworks. Skill in interpreting results and ensuring adherence to physical laws. Course Learning Outcomes: | By the end of this course students will be able to:
Understand neural network fundamentals and physics-based integration. Solve physics-related problems using Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs). Formulate and solve PDEs with neural networks. Apply PINNs to real-world physics applications. Optimize and evaluate PINNs for performance and accuracy. Design and implement custom PINN models. 2. Goals, Objectives, and Learning Outcomes of the Course | 2. Goals, Objectives, and Learning Outcomes of the Course
Course Description | Computer Vision has become ubiquitous in our society, with applications in search, image understanding, apps, mapping, medicine, drones, and self-driving cars. Core to many of these applications are visual recognition tasks such as image classification, localization and detection. Recent developments in neural network (aka “deep learning”) approaches have greatly advanced the performance of these state-of-the-art visual recognition systems. This course is a deep dive into the details of deep learning architectures with a focus on learning end-to-end models for these tasks, particularly image classification. During the 10-week course, students will learn to implement and train their own neural networks and gain a detailed understanding of cutting-edge research in computer vision. Course Goal(s) | Course goal is to provide a solid background in computer vision and deep learning, in preparation either for a job in industry or for more advanced courses at the graduate level. Course Objectives: | Course objectives include:
To understand basics of traditional computer vision and data driven computer vision; To understand basics of machine learning; To understand the definition of a range of neural network models; To understand optimization algorithms for neural network models; To understand and implement various neural network algorithms in a range of real-world vision applications. Skills & Competences | Programming. Analytical. Problem solving. Critical thinking. Communication. Course Learning Outcomes: | Upon completion of the course the student should have the following learning outcomes defined in terms of knowledge, skills and general competence:
explain the basic principles behind neural networks and deep learning;
compare modeling aspects of various neural network architectures;
implement simple neural network algorithms;
apply and evaluate deep learning on real data sets;
provide successful examples how deep learning can be used in different contexts in the society;
read and critically assess papers on artificial neural networks and their applications.

Course Description | Deep Learning has revolutionized fields like computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and autonomous systems. Its applications span from powering recommendation systems and voice assistants to advancing medical diagnostics and generative AI. At the core of these breakthroughs are deep neural networks, capable of learning intricate patterns from massive datasets. This course provides an in-depth exploration of deep learning, focusing on its foundational principles, modern architectures, and practical implementations. Topics include neural network design, optimization techniques, and advanced models like convolutional and recurrent neural networks. Over the span of 10 weeks, students will build, train, and fine-tune deep learning models using popular frameworks. By the end of the course, students will gain hands-on experience and a solid understanding of state-of-the-art methods shaping the future of artificial intelligence. Course Goal(s) | The goal of this course is to provide students with a robust foundation in deep learning, equipping them with the skills and knowledge necessary for industry roles in artificial intelligence or for pursuing advanced studies and research at the graduate level. Students will develop a deep understanding of neural network architectures, training methodologies, and cutting-edge applications across various domains. Course Objectives: | The objectives of this deep learning course are:
To understand the fundamental concepts of deep learning and neural networks. To explore the basics of supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning approaches. To gain knowledge of key deep learning architectures, including convolutional, recurrent, and transformer networks. To understand and apply optimization techniques for training deep learning models effectively. To implement and deploy deep learning solutions for real-world applications across various domains. Explore and apply convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for image classification and feature extraction. Analyze and compare different CNN architectures, such as AlexNet, VGG, ResNet, and EfficientNet. Understand and implement recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and their variants (LSTMs, GRUs) for sequential data processing. Gain a deep understanding of the attention mechanism and Transformer models, including their applications in NLP and vision tasks. Explore Vision-Language Models (VLMs) and their applications in multimodal AI tasks. Skills & Competences | Programming. Analytical. Problem solving. Critical thinking. Communication. Course Learning Outcomes: | By the end of this course, students will be able to:
Understand the fundamental principles of neural networks and deep learning.

Methodological Guidelines        
Assessment is administered continuously throughout the course. The students are rated against their performance in continuous rating administered throughout the semester (60%) and summative rating done during the examination session (40%), total 100%. Continuous rating is students’ on-going performance in class and independent work. Class work is assessed for attendance, laboratory works' defense and in- class assessments. The ideas from Calculus I and II are applicable to numerous fields, including engineering, physics, mathematics, biology, and many others.
